source: Yadav 2022 Iran J Child Neurol (PMID 35222658, PMC open access); NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
note: Open-label randomised, 52 recruited and 48 analysed per protocol, comparator syrup held calcium and vitamin D without magnesium, no blinding. No post-treatment serum magnesium is reported in the text read although the Discussion says supplementation raised it. The EEG p value is not reproducible from Table 2 (about 0.10 by a Fisher test), EEG denominators differ (26 and 22), and Table 3's margins agree with Table 2 once its unlabelled 'Low' row (4/2/3, printed in the table footer of the XML) is assigned to the non-intervention group by the group totals (an earlier reading that they disagreed assigned that row to the intervention group; corrected 2026-11-25, ADV-276, after a blind check). Table 3's printed p values (0.003 intervention, 0.42 non-intervention) reproduce by chi-square from the counts (0.0029 and 0.418; intervention Low 4/4/0 and Normal 2/3/13, non-intervention Low 4/2/3 and Normal 3/2/8); Table 4's 0.004 and the seizure-control 0.69 also reproduce, and only the EEG p value of Table 2 does not.

source: ChEMBL_37 assay descriptions of document CHEMBL6083260 (PMID 39442339, abstract only; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE)
note: One closed patch-clamp document lists inhibitory concentrations of both blockers that are far higher at a holding potential 20 mV more depolarised. The size of the shift is physically implausible for a single-site pore block (at most about two-fold per 20 mV is expected) and may reflect protocol, solution or transcription; the paper was not opened and the figures are UNVERIFIED and not used in the card's argument. Voltage dependence of pore block is real in direction, and a burst is a depolarising event, so a potency measured at one voltage is not a burst-state potency.

source: Banke et al 2026, Brain (PMID 40994429; partial full text read 2026-11-25, ADV-276, receipt FTR-20261125-40994429-01; supplements not held; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE)
note: Receptor-level evidence for a gain-of-function lesion, where the sign is known. It does not show an effect in a WWOX system, and a GluN2B NAM acts on GluN2B-containing receptors only (the organoid shows GRIN2B and GRIN2D transcripts). Full text (ADV-276, 2026-11-25): radiprodil was equally or more effective than at wild type in 22 of 27 variants by potency (printed) and in 21 of 27 (77.8 percent) when maximal inhibition is also counted (our count from Table 2, not printed; the one addition is I150V, which keeps potency but reaches 31 percent maximal inhibition against 85 percent at wild type). S810R, the variant of the mouse model, is one of five potency losses: the text prints 1.9-fold; Table 2 gives a ratio of about 1.5 against the pooled wild type (the printed fold changes are not reproducible from the pooled value, and one paragraph reverses the two values). S810R mice, radiprodil or vehicle, then pentylenetetrazole 30 minutes later (Table 3; doses in the paper): latency to first myoclonic jerk 131 +/- 33 s (n = 26) against 99 +/- 8.4 s (vehicle; n = 21 in the Results text, 20 in Table 3), P = 0.40; latency to generalised tonic-clonic seizure 458 +/- 90 s (the 16 mice that seized) against 207 +/- 23 s (the 20 that seized), mean +/- SEM, P = 0.0053 by unpaired t-test among animals that seized; 16 of 26 radiprodil mice against 20 of 21 vehicle mice seized (Fisher two-sided 0.013, our computation, not printed). Wild-type littermates: 6 of 18 radiprodil against 5 of 21 vehicle seized. The direction DECREASE stays at receptor level; the seizure endpoint is incidence and latency among animals that seized, not a general delay.
